question.worked_solution:
First we apply the quotient rule, subtracting exponents in the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{5}\cdot \frac{{a}^{-3}}{{a}^{2}} & = \\ {a}^{5}\cdot {a}^{(-3-2)} & = \\ {a}^{5}\cdot {a}^{-5} & \end{aligned}
$$

Then we apply the product rule, adding exponents in the product:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{a}^{5}\cdot {a}^{-5} & = \\ {a}^{5+(-5)} & = \\ {a}^{5-5} & = \\ {a}^{0} & = \\ 1 & \end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{a}^{5}\cdot \frac{{a}^{-3}}{{a}^{2}}=1.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
